title: Reti vs Tartakower
summary: Reti's win against Tartakower is remembered for its short, sharp finish: a queen sacrifice on d8 and a bishop mate after Black's 8...Nxe4 blunder turned a level position into mate in three. Watch how White's open d-file and the king's exposure on c7 combine, and how Black's early queen check cost time.

moves.comment: 1.e4 takes the centre and opens lines for the queen and bishop, the most natural start for club players.
1...c6 prepares ...d5 with a sound pawn structure. The engine preferred 1...e5, followed by 2.Nf3.
2.d4 adds a second central pawn, building the broad centre that White wants.
2...d5 challenges the centre directly, and this is the best reply in the engine's view.
3.Nc3 develops and adds pressure on d5. The engine preferred 3.e5 followed by 3...Bf5.
3...dxe4 releases the tension and wins a pawn for the moment. The engine rates this as the best move.
4.Nxe4 recaptures and centralises the knight. Material is level again and the position stays balanced.
4...Nf6 develops and attacks the knight. The engine preferred 4...Bf5, developing the bishop first.
5.Qd3 brings the queen out early, eyeing h7 and the d-file. The engine preferred 5.Nxf6+ to trade off the attacker first.
5...e5 opens the centre at a cost. The engine preferred 5...Nxe4, and this pawn push is an inaccuracy that lets White's pieces come alive.

moment.title: Opening the centre too early
moment.text: Black's 5...e5 pushes a pawn into the open centre while White's pieces are ready. The engine preferred 5...Nxe4, which trades pieces and keeps the position calm. This is marked as an inaccuracy because it gives White a target and lines to use.

moves.comment: 6.dxe5 opens the d-file towards Black's king and keeps the initiative. The engine rates it as the best move.
6...Qa5+ gives check but only gains a little time. The engine preferred 6...Qxd3, trading queens, so this is an inaccuracy.

moment.title: Check that gains only time
moment.text: 6...Qa5+ looks active, but the queen is pulled offside and White gains a tempo with Bd2. The engine preferred 6...Qxd3 to trade queens. Checks like this are useful only when they lead somewhere concrete.

moves.comment: 7.Bd2 blocks the check with a developing move. It is the best reply and keeps White's queen and king safe for now.
7...Qxe5 regains the pawn and is the best move. White still keeps a clear advantage in the evaluation.
8.O-O-O castles long, placing the rook on the open d-file behind the queen. The engine rates this as the best move.

moment.title: Rook to the open file
moment.text: 8.O-O-O puts the rook on the d-file, which is now open, lined up against Black's king. White's king is also safe on the queenside. The evaluation sits at about plus 1.8, so White has a comfortable edge.

moves.comment: 8...Nxe4 grabs a knight but walks into a forced mating attack. This is a blunder; the engine preferred 8...Be7 and the evaluation swings to mate in three.

moment.title: The decisive blunder
moment.text: 8...Nxe4 wins material at first glance but allows a forced attack on the d-file. The evaluation jumps from plus 1.8 to mate in three. The engine preferred 8...Be7, which would have kept Black in the game.

moves.comment: 9.Qd8+ sacrifices the queen to deflect the king. This is the best move and the engine now sees mate in two.

moment.title: Queen sacrifice opens the net
moment.text: 9.Qd8+ gives up the queen to pull the king onto d8. The next checks leave Black with no time to defend. The engine shows the sequence as mate in two after this move.

moves.comment: 9...Kxd8 takes the queen, which is the natural reply, but the engine still shows mate in two.
10.Bg5+ checks the king and drives it towards the centre. The engine rates this as best and shows mate in one next.
10...Kc7 steps towards safety, but the engine still shows mate in one after this move.
11.Bd8# delivers mate with the bishop, ending the game with the king on c7 unable to escape.

moment.title: Mate on d8
moment.text: 11.Bd8# finishes the game with the bishop delivering mate. Each earlier check forced the king further forward. This is a clear illustration of checks leading to mate.

lessons: Before grabbing material, check whether the capture opens a file or diagonal towards your king.
Use checks only when they lead to a concrete gain, because a check that merely wastes time can hand the opponent the initiative.
When your opponent's king is in the centre with open files, look for sacrifices and forcing checks that drive it into the open.
